name: warp
summary: Full-bleed hero running Paper Shaders' warp on WebGL2: a checked pattern swirled ten times into itself until it reads as lit ridges turning through a dark violet liquid.

colors.description: Up to ten stops. The upstream preset alternates near-black with violet, which is what makes the output read as lit ridges in a dark liquid rather than as a four-way blend. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

speed.description: Rate the liquid turns over. 0 renders a single static frame. Forced to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

distortion.description: How far the underlying pattern is pushed out of shape before the swirl.

swirl.description: How hard the field is twisted around itself. 0 leaves the pattern legible as a grid.

softness.description: Edge softness between the stops. 0 gives hard-edged shapes instead of a liquid.

deviations.what: The noise texture is decoded before ShaderMount is constructed, so the shader starts one microtask later than a React mount would.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream's React component hands getShaderNoiseTexture() straight to ShaderMount and re-renders when it loads; a vanilla mount has no re-render, and ShaderMount throws on an image that is not complete. The image is a data: URI, so nothing is fetched.
